title: Protect women from violence in public places
article: A recent spate of violent attacks against women in public places shows the need for colleagues and onlookers to play a greater role in stopping and reporting domestic abuse, critics said Wednesday.

Disturbingly bold incidents like those that played out this week in Ontario point to an unsettling level of complacency among politicians who are supposed to enact laws that protect women, suggested one human-rights lawyer.

Geri Sanson said the public nature of two recent slayings and a shooting says a lot about "the perceived consequences or the degree to which our culture (has) complacency or a lack of accountability."
Co-workers watched in horror Tuesday as Peter Francis, 34, twice shot his estranged wife before police shot and killed him in the parking lot of a factory in east-end Toronto.
Francis wounded his wife Rayness, 48, in the leg and abdomen as she arrived for work at an auto-parts maker.
"Generally speaking, as a community we could all do a lot more than we're doing," said Pam Cross, co-ordinator of the Ontario Women's Justice Network.

Such involvement may include cautioning workers against using misogynistic language and fostering a safe and welcoming work environment for women who may consider the office a refuge from a volatile home.
